gaps.lead: I'd like to move to a place where nobody knows me.
gaps.sentence: I'd like to move ___ nobody knows me.

gaps.lead: Brian was really interested in North American history in his school days.
gaps.sentence: Brian ___ North American history in his school days.
gaps.hint: be interested in = have an ___ in
gaps.explanation: 'To be interested in' becomes the noun pattern: 'had an interest in'.

gaps.lead: Living in the city is new to her.
gaps.sentence: She is not ___ in the city.
gaps.explanation: 'Be used to living' = be accustomed to (note the gerund).

gaps.lead: Although he is remarkably rich, he lives very simply.
gaps.explanation: Although he may be rich → Rich as (he) may be — fronted adjective + as + may.

gaps.lead: I have never read such a gripping novel.
gaps.sentence: This is ___ I have ever read.
gaps.explanation: 'Never read such a gripping novel' = 'the most gripping novel I have ever read'.

gaps.lead: I don't expect the company to make a profit this year, given the economic climate.
gaps.sentence: Given the economic climate, ___ the company made a profit this year.
gaps.hint: don't expect = would be surprised if + past
gaps.explanation: A tentative prediction: 'I would be surprised if + past simple'.
